Abandoning this as we are waiting for the internal team updates.
SSE and websockets already handle this case?  Maybe talk in terms of what you're trying to enable?

Hi @ed@tanous.net The intent of this change is not to alter existing privilege behavior, but to decouple privilege handling from HTTP rule parameter parsing so it can be reused uniformly across different connection types. Extracting privilege handling into PrivilegeParameterTraits allows common privilege configuration logic
Please add that to your commit msg. Your commit msg doesn't have a "Why" at this time.

> Extracting privilege handling into PrivilegeParameterTraits allows common privilege configuration logic

Please also point to an example of what this means.

Hi @ed@tanous.net RuleParameterTraits bundles HTTP-specific methods (methods(), notFound(), etc.) with privilege configuration. Non-HTTP connection types like SseSocketRule and WebSocketRule inherit only BaseRule and cannot configure privileges without pulling in all that HTTP-specific logic. By extracting privileges into PrivilegeParameterTraits, these types can inherit just the privilege API — e.g., class SseSocketRule : public BaseRule, public PrivilegeParameterTraits<SseSocketRule> — without unrelated HTTP routing methods. RuleParameterTraits itself then inherits PrivilegeParameterTraits to preserve existing behavior.
